title: Key-Takeaway & Sub-Concept Coverage (no gaps, no scope creep)
description: The generated TR doc must teach EVERY key takeaway of the session as per the curriculum AND the exam-testable sub-concepts inside each one, and must NOT introduce scope beyond them. Two layers, and the first is new: the curriculum line itself is a CONTRACT — it is written as "Topic: item; item, item", and every item after the colon is owed to the learner, so each must be taught in that takeaway's section (a deterministic guardrail now checks exactly this, matching on distinctive vocabulary and treating any acronym the line names as mandatory). Second, a syllabus line names a topic, not its scope, so the doc's `coverage_map` must enumerate the exam-testable sub-concepts and map each to the slide teaching it or to a named deferral. The map is VERIFIED, not trusted: a thin map that restates the takeaway, or one pointing at a slide that does not teach that sub-concept, fails. Deferral is a last resort — never for something the line names, never to make room, and never for most of a takeaway (that is a postponed takeaway, not a taught one). The session must be COMPLETE when it ends: every takeaway delivered, nothing dangling.
criterion: Every sub-topic named in the curriculum's takeaway line is taught in that takeaway's section; every takeaway has a coverage_map entry with the sub-concepts an exam would test; every sub-concept resolves to a slide that genuinely teaches it, or to an explicitly named deferral that belongs to a later session; nothing is taught outside the takeaway set.

rubric.5: All takeaways, every sub-topic their lines name, and their standard sub-concepts covered; coverage_map accurate; zero scope creep.
rubric.3: All covered but one sub-concept is thin, or one minor out-of-scope aside.
rubric.1: A sub-topic the curriculum line names, a whole takeaway, or a commonly-tested sub-concept is missing (silently, behind a map entry that does not hold up, or behind a deferral used to make room), or a whole section is out of scope.
